title: Speed: NEAT networks compiled to NumPy; orphaned test runs found
text:
Profiling showed 70% of training time inside neat-python's network evaluation (pure Python, one connection at a time). FastNet compiles each genome into one NumPy matrix product per layer; same outputs to 1e-9 and identical flights (tested). Clean timing per simulated step: network 100 -> about 20 us, sensors 11 us, env.step 58 us of which Box2D's C++ physics is only 1.5 us. Run K: 111 -> 68 s per generation.
A full C++ rebuild of the flight could be 8-10x faster but would take 1-2 days and must reproduce gymnasium exactly, or every comparison breaks; not worth it with 4.5 days left.
Also found: three smoke-test trainers left running by timed-out tests, two of them for 7.5 hours, taking CPU from real training. Killed; the test now kills its whole process group. And a restart of mine waited on a pgrep pattern that matched its own shell, leaving K stopped for ~25 minutes; restart_run.sh now uses anchored patterns.

title: The wrecking ball: NEAT's structural mutations. Attempt K mutates gently
text:
Run J (landing-first fitness) drifted less but still down: 87% at gen 0, about 75% on average over gens 5-70; the population's mean fitness fell from 304 to 110-190, a sign that most children are damaged.
Measured directly (experiments/mutation_damage.py, 12 children of the start network, 150 real-task flights each; start 86.0%):
  stock settings (weights 0.4 x 0.05): children 70.5% on average, worst 7%, 10/12 more than 5 points worse
  weights only 0.2 x 0.02: 73.4%, still 8/12 worse; even 0.05 x 0.005: 74.7%, 8/12 worse
  gentle (no weight/bias replacement, no on/off toggles, connection deletion 1%, node add 1%) + 0.2 x 0.02: 83.4%, worst 79%, 2/12 worse
So the damage came from the structural and replacement mutations, not the nudges: replacing a trained weight of up to +-20 with a fresh random one, or switching a connection off, wrecks the network.
Attempt K = J with neat-config-gentle.ini, fresh from the clone.

note: Attempt K = J (real task only, landing-first fitness, from the pilot-v2 clone) with one change: gentle mutation (neat-config-gentle.ini). J still drifted from 87% to ~75%; measured on the start network (86%), one stock NEAT mutation leaves children at 70.5% on average (10/12 more than 5 points worse, worst 7%), mostly from weight replacement, connection toggles and deletions. Gentle settings: 83.4% (2/12 worse, worst 79%).

expect: Children no longer wrecked, so the population should hold ~85% and selection can find the rare improvements.

title: Reward trap found: points up, landings down. Attempt J pays for landings
text:
Run I (real task only, from the pilot-v2 clone) drifted down too: real-task champion 85% (gen 0) -> 58-83%, about 72% on average over gens 5-75. So it was not the curriculum. Meanwhile the champion's game score ROSE (182 -> 210-220). The fitness was game score + 100 per landing + up to 50 for the centre; the game score pays for saving fuel and for flying to the centre, and evolution traded landings for points.
Attempt J (one change, the fitness): +300 for landing between the flags, no centre bonus, game score x 0.3 as a tie-breaker, -100 extra for a boulder hit, -200 for a timeout. Fresh from the clone.

note: Attempt J = I with one change: the fitness rewards landing, not points. In I the champion's game score rose (182 -> 210-220) while its real-task landing rate fell (85% -> ~72% on 100 fresh flights): the score pays for fuel economy and the centre bonus, a trap. Now: +300 for landing between the flags, no centre bonus, game score x 0.3 as a tie-breaker, -100 extra for a boulder hit, -200 for a timeout. Fresh from the pilot-v2 clone.

expect: Selection now pays for landings. Expect the real-task line to hold at ~85% and then climb; if it still drifts down, the next suspect is mutation noise.

note: Attempt I: start from the pilot-v2 clone (84.8% real task) and train ONLY on the real task. Why: in H the real-task result fell from 83% (gen 0) to 58-61% by gen 25 in the 'boulder, calm air' stage, despite 40% rehearsal; the clone leans on the clean wind sensor, which reads ~0 in calm air, so those weights drift. Same lesson as B-D: with an expert start, any world but the real one erodes skill. 24 flights per network, re-fly top 8 on 60.

expect: Hold the clone's ~85% and push the remaining failures (boulder hits, off-pad, crashes, ~4-5% each) down. Pass = 98% on 100 + 100 fresh flights, then the 1,000-flight goal check.

title: H erodes the new start; attempt I trains on the real task only
text:
Run H (pilot-v2 clone, curriculum around the boulder with 40% rehearsal): the champion on 100 fresh real-task flights fell from 83% (gen 0) to 70, 60, 69, 61, 58% (gens 5-25), boulder hits 7% -> 15%. The clone relies on the clean wind sensor; in calm air it reads ~0, so its weights drift unpunished, and 40% rehearsal can't hold them. Same lesson as runs B-D: with an expert start, every world that isn't the real task erodes skill.
Attempt I: the same clone, one stage, only the real task, 24 flights per network (re-fly top 8 on 60). The cleanest test of whether NEAT can improve on its start.

title: Breakthrough: pilot v2 lands 86% on the real task; attempt H starts from its clone
text:
Tuning pilot v2 (with the clean wind sensor) on the corrected final task, 40 rounds of CMA-ES, worked where tuning v1 hadn't. On 600 paired unseen real-task flights: v2 tuned 86.3% vs v1 74.7% (+11.7, 95% CI +8.2 to +15.3); off the pad 29 vs 74, crashed 24 vs 36, boulder 24 vs 37. Plain wind: 97.0% vs 92.7%.
Cloned with DAgger (7 rounds, 1.7 million steps, 92.7% agreement) into a 16-24-4 network. As an exact NEAT genome it lands 84.8% on the real task vs the pilot's 85.2% on the same 600 flights (no real difference), and 96.3% in plain wind.
Route sensors are pinned to the v1 margins they were built with (lander/route_params.json), so older networks see the same inputs.
G stopped (it stayed at 55-79%). Attempt H starts from the v2 clone, under the supervisor. Generation 0: 83% on 100 fresh real-task flights.

note: Attempt H: a new start. The pilot v2 (clean wind sensor, edge clamp, early brake, tuned on the corrected final task) cloned into a 16-24-4 network. Same curriculum as F (boulder in calm air -> in gusts -> everything -> polish, 40% real-task rehearsal, 20 flights per network), with one rule change: a stage passes with <= 2% boulder hits on the check (zero hits blocked checks of 96-98% landed).

expect: The pilot lands 95.6% here. The copy should get there; selection now sees the boulder in every flight.

title: G paused to give the pilot tuning the CPU
text: Run G (on the corrected boulder) hasn't improved on the real task: 55-71% on 100 fresh flights since gen 345. Paused (SIGSTOP, nothing lost) so the pilot-v2 tuning gets the whole CPU; it will resume afterwards or give way to attempt H.

title: A clean wind sensor: correlation with the true wind 0.14 -> 0.97
text:
The user extended full autonomy to Wednesday 17:00. Plan: NEAT keeps its start network's skill but has not improved on it, so build a much better start.
Step 1, the wind sensor. In calm air I measured each action's sideways push per step: nothing 0 (noise 0.0003), side engines -0.0098 / +0.0098 (noise 0.0015), main engine -0.071 x sin(tilt) (noise 0.0105, as big as a full gust of 0.012). The old drift sensor kept main-engine steps and ignored their push: over 40 flights it correlates only 0.14 with the true (hidden) wind. A new sensor subtracts each action's known push and trusts main-engine steps 10x less: correlation 0.97, rms error 0.17 gust units. It is input 16 (wind_est); older 15-input networks ignore it.
Step 2, pilot v2: leans on wind_est, keeps detour targets within |x| <= 0.7, and brakes when a boulder is close below. Untuned, on 600 paired unseen flights: real task 78.3% vs 74.7% (+3.7, CI +0.2 to +7.3), plain wind 95.5% vs 92.7%. Now tuning its 16 gains with CMA-ES on the corrected final task.

expect: The full final world. Start level with the pilot (~71-77%); aim to pass it.

title: Overnight crash, a flaw in my boulder, and the fix
text:
1) Run F crashed at 21:14 with an AssertionError in neat-python (get_new_node_key): after a resume, the counter for new node keys restarted from one genome's highest key and collided with another genome's. Nothing caught it until 08:40, about 11 hours of compute lost; the scheduled check-ins didn't fire overnight. Fixed in train.py with a test, and runs now go through supervise.sh, which restarts a crashed trainer from its checkpoint and logs the crash on this page.
2) Tuning the pilot on the final task (CMA-ES, 40 rounds) gained little: 78.5% vs 75.7% on 600 paired flights (+2.8, CI -0.5 to +6.3), and it got worse in plain wind. The pilot's gains are at their ceiling.
3) Mapping failures by boulder position showed a flaw in the obstacle I designed: the boulder's top could sit 1.7 m below the start, the lander fell onto it within 1-3 seconds, and even a hard escape manoeuvre still hit it in 2.1% of flights. With 98% as the goal, that left no room. With the user's approval the boulder's top now stays at least 3.5 m below the start (the crude escape now fails 0.65%). Lower boulders crowd the pad: on the new layout the pilot lands 71.7% (off the pad 14%) and F's best champion 72.3%.
Attempt G = F's population on the corrected task.

note: Attempt G = F resumed, with one change, approved by the user: a fairer boulder. Its top now stays at least 3.5 m below the start (centre 3 m above the pad up to 6.5 m minus its radius; it was up to 7 m). Before, about 2% of flights put the rock right under the start and looked unavoidable (a crude escape still hit 2.1%; now 0.65%). Lower boulders crowd the pad more: the pilot lands 71.7% on the new layout. All real-task numbers from here on are on the new layout.

AssertionError in neat-python get_new_node_key: after a resume, new node keys could collide with existing ones. Not noticed until 08:40 the next morning (~11 hours lost). Fixed in train.py (with a test); a supervisor now restarts crashed runs.

title: Real task flat at ~71%; tuning the pilot on the final task
text:
Run F (20 flights per network) in 'boulder, gusts': the champion on 100 fresh real-task flights every 5 generations, gens 245-325: 59% to 80%, about 71% on average, no trend; the pilot lands ~77%. Stage-world checks reach 92-98% but fail on 1-2% boulder hits. So NEAT keeps the start network's skill but hasn't improved on it, with 10 or 20 flights per network.
The start network is what decides the result so far, and the pilot it copies was tuned on half wind / half boulder flights, not the final task. Side experiment (F keeps running): CMA-ES tunes the pilot's 13 gains on the final task only (40 rounds x 16 candidates x 160 flights, seeds 600M+). If it clearly beats the current pilot on paired analysis flights, the next attempt re-clones from it.

title: Finding: the drift sensor mostly feels the lander's own thrust
text:
Building the 'How it sees' page, I plotted the true wind force (hidden from the lander) against its drift sensor over a whole flight. The sensor swings between about -3 and +3 while the true wind stays within +-1 (in units of a full gust). The sensor leaves out side-engine steps but keeps main-engine steps, so when the lander is tilted its own main engine dominates the reading. It is a 'total sideways push' accelerometer, not a wind estimate.
It still helped the pilot (72% -> 94%), but a cleaner sensor would subtract the known sideways thrust of the main engine (from the tilt and the action). A candidate change if progress stalls; not changed now (one change at a time).

title: Rehearsal keeps the boulder skill; selection noise stops progress. Attempt F
text:
Run E (curriculum around the boulder, 40% real-task rehearsal) stage 1 hit its cap: best fresh check 96% landed but 3% boulder hits (the pass needs 0).
Paired on 400 unseen real-task flights: gen 75 champion 76.2%, gen 140 70.0%, pilot 76.8%. So rehearsal works in part: D had fallen to 38%, E stays near the pilot. But it doesn't pass the pilot, and full-wind skill still slipped (gen 140: 80.0% vs pilot 92.3%).
Failure breakdown (gen 75, real task): crashed 12.8%, boulder 7.0%, off-pad 5.8%, timeout 1.8%; the pilot: off-pad 10.5%, boulder 7.0%, crashed 6.8%.
Diagnosis: with 10 flights per network, 4 of them real, selection can't tell 76% from 70%; later champions looked better on the stage world but were worse on the real one.
Change (one): attempt F resumes E's population at the start of stage 2 with 20 flights per network and the top 8 re-flown on 60.

Why: in the real task E's champions did not pass the pilot and drifted down (gen 75: 76.2%, gen 140: 70.0%, pilot 76.8%, 400 paired flights) while their stage-world checks rose: selection on 10 flights (4 of them real) is mostly luck.

title: The easy stages were erasing skill. Attempt E: curriculum around the weakness, with rehearsal
text:
Run D passed calm air (gen 5) and the steady push (gen 91, 90% / 91%). But paired against the pilot on 300 unseen flights, D's champions got WORSE at the real task as the stages went on:
  full wind: gen 0 90.3% (pilot 92.3%), gen 5 78.7%, gen 91 52.0%
  with the boulder: gen 0 71.0% (pilot 76.7%), gen 91 38.0%
Selection only sees the stage's easy world, so mutations erode the hard-world skill with nothing to stop them. A curriculum that helps a beginner hurts an expert start.
Attempt E (one change: the curriculum): restart from the exact copy; train the weakness, the boulder, from calm air up (boulder in calm air -> boulder in gusts -> everything -> polish); and fly 40% of every stage's training flights in the full final world (rehearsal), so selection always sees the real task.

expect: Real gusts at full strength. The wind project's best NEAT reached ~91% with turbulence; aim 95% without.
Lean into a constant push that grows from 5 to 15. The pilot lands ~84-90% here, so pass at 90%. Risk: landing off the pad downwind.

note: Attempt D: restart forced by a bug. Runs A-C started from a broken copy of the pilot: NEAT's tanh output squashed the cloned scores to ties, so 1 step in 9 took the wrong action (the copy landed 43% in wind instead of 92%). Fixed (identity outputs, test). Restarting, so three more changes ride along: the 15-input clone (+2 route sensors), seed noise 0.02 and weight mutation power 0.05 (the boulder skill is fragile: noise 0.05 cost ~10 points), and 30% boulder flights mixed into stages 1-4 so selection keeps protecting the boulder skill (forgotten twice before). The exact start network: 98% wind, 77% boulder (60 flights each).

expect: Pass at once: the exact copy of the pilot lands nearly every calm flight.

title: Bug found: NEAT started from a broken copy. Attempt D
text:
While checking why the boulder skill was missing, I compared the cloned network flown directly with the same network converted into a NEAT genome. With the boulder: 71% vs 30%. In wind: 92% vs 43%. The conversion was not exact: NEAT's tanh output neurons squashed the cloned action scores (up to +-20) to exactly 1.0, and the first of a tie won. About 1 step in 9 took the wrong action. The unit test missed it because a random small network never saturates.
Correction: episode 1 said NEAT started from a copy landing ~82%. The genome NEAT actually got was much worse; runs A-C's stage results are real measurements, but they were achieved from a broken start.
Fix: identity output neurons (exact copy), test now uses realistic weights and fails without the fix. The exact 15-input copy: 98% wind, 77% boulder (60 flights each, rough).
Attempt D restarts from it, with three changes riding along on the forced restart: 2 route sensors (15 inputs), gentler mutation (seed noise 0.02, weight power 0.05: noise 0.05 cost ~10 points with the boulder), and 30% boulder flights mixed into stages 1-4.

expect: Everything on, only the env score + landing bonus. Pass = 98% on 100 + 100 fresh flights, then the 1,000-flight goal check.
Starts near 14-25% landed with full-size boulders, so ramp the size 40% -> 100% over 150 generations. Expect the longest stage; a pass at 95% may need the polish stage too.

title: Gusts passed; full wind below the pilot; boulder skill missing; attempt C
text:
Gusts (no turbulence) passed at generation 202: 96% on 100 fresh flights, confirmed.
Full wind (gusts 15 + turbulence 1.5): the best fresh check was 92% (gen 373), but that was partly selection luck. On 400 paired unseen flights the same champion lands 86.0% vs the pilot's 91.0% (-5.0 [-9.2, -0.8]). The gusts champion: 71.8%. So turbulence is the hard part of the wind, and NEAT is still below its teacher there.
Bigger problem, found by checking ahead: with the boulder, the best champion lands 14.3% and even the cloned start network only 25.0%, vs the pilot's 76.7% (300 paired flights). The boulder rules (steer beside it, stay above it) never made it into the clone.
Change (one): attempt C resumes B's population at gen 417 and ramps the boulder size from 40% to 100% over the first half of the boulder stage, the way wind was ramped.

note: Attempt C = B resumed from its population at gen ~412 (in the gusts + turbulence stage), with one change: the boulder stage ramps the boulder size from 40% to 100%. Why: the cloned start network only landed 25% with the boulder (pilot 77%) and B's best wind champion 14% (300 paired flights): the boulder skill was never cloned well, so it must be learned in NEAT, from small boulders up.

expect: The full wind task. Beat the earlier 91%.

title: Steady push passed, beating the pilot, but it forgot the gusts
text:
Run B passed the steady-push stage at generation 76: 99% landed on 100 fresh flights, 96% on the confirmation.
Paired with the hand-written pilot on the same 300 unseen flights against a full-strength constant push: champion 97.3%, pilot 82.3%, difference +15.0 points [95% CI +10.7, +19.3]. NEAT beat its teacher.
But in the real gusty wind with turbulence the same champion lands only 64.3% vs the pilot's 92.3% (-28.0 [-34.0, -22.0]): it specialised in a constant push. The gusts stage (now running, wind ramping 5 -> 15) has to win that back. If it doesn't, the steady-push stage should be shortened or mixed with real gusts.

title: Attempt A stopped, B started: a bug and weaker training wheels
text:
Run A passed calm air at generation 5 (98% and 97% on two fresh sets of 100), but in the steady-push stage the champion fell to 72-80% landed already at 'wind 5'. Two causes, both measured with the pilot on 200 flights:
1. A bug: the steady push ignored the wind ramp and was always 30-100% of full strength. Fixed, with a test.
2. Training wheels at full strength hurt: the pilot landed 83% with them, 84% without, 89.5% at 0.3 strength. They stop the lander tilting to steer.
Attempt B: wheels start at 0.3, steady-push pass at 90%. Restarted from the cloned network (stage 1 took only 3 minutes).

expect: The drift sensor should let it lean into a constant push. Risk: landing off the pad downwind.

title: Kickoff: NEAT seeded with a cloned pilot
text:
Goal: >= 98% landed between the flags on 1,000 unseen flights with wind 15, turbulence 1.5 and a floating boulder, by Wednesday 4 November 18:00.

Built today: the world (wind seeded per flight, the boulder as a static rock, training wheels), a hand-written pilot tuned with CMA-ES (500 unseen flights: calm 100% landed, wind+turbulence 93.8%, with the boulder 74.2%), and a 13-24-4 network cloned from it with DAgger (about 82% landed over mixed worlds). Every genome in NEAT's first population is a copy of that network with small noise; its 24 hidden neurons are protected from deletion.

Run A started: six stages (calm, steady push, gusts, turbulence, boulder, polish). Generation 0 already landed 99% on 100 fresh calm flights.

note: NEAT from a cloned teacher network (24 hidden), six stages: calm, steady push, gusts, turbulence, boulder, polish. Training wheels fade in stages 2-4.

expect: Quick: the cloned network already lands in calm air; NEAT polishes centring. Pass within ~30 generations.
